case_name: Kailash Chand Sharma v State of Rajasthan and Others
facts: The Judgment was delivered by : P. Venkatarama Reddi, J.

At the outset, it may be stated that the judgment of the full Bench rendered on 21 October 1999 in Deepak Kumar's case (1999(2), RLR 692) was in relation to the selection of teachers Grade II and Grade III which was pursuant to the advertisement issued by the Director, Primary and Secondary Education during the year 1995.
The said posts of teachers Grade II and Grade III are borne in State cadre under the administrative control of Education Department of the State Government.

What was called in question by the unsuccessful candidates who filed their applications and appeared before the o.1 Selection Boards was the award of bonus marks to the applicants belonging to the District and the rural areas of the district concerned.
The first full Bench (in the case of Deepak Kumar Vs. State) held that award of such bonus marks was unconstitutional and the relevant clause in the circular providing for bonus marks was void.
Having so declared the law, the full Bench gave the following directions in the concluding para of the judgment :-
It is this decision that was followed by the full Bench in the impugned judgment and the batch of Writ Petitions were disposed of accordingly.

After the full Bench judgment one more batch of writ petitions came to be disposed of by a learned single Judge of the High Court on 26 February 2001 directing a fresh merit list to be prepared in respect of the candidates who were not appointed on or before 21 October 1999 without regard to the bonus marks.
The Chief Executive Officers-cum-Secretaries of Zila Parishads were required to issue the advertisements by 15 June 1998 and to have them published in the newspapers by 20 June 1998.
Accordingly, the learned single Judge suggested to the learned Chief Justice to constitute full Bench.

To recapitulate the sequence, it may be noted that the first full Bench decision in Deepak Kumar's case relating to appointments in the Education Department was decided on 21 October 1999 The second full Bench dealing with the cases on hand gave its verdict on 18 November 1999.
In this factual background, the S.L.Ps came to be filed in this Court.
issues: What was called in question by the unsuccessful candidates who filed their applications and appeared before the o.1 Selection Boards was the award of bonus marks to the applicants belonging to the District and the rural areas of the district concerned.
The first full Bench (in the case of Deepak Kumar Vs. State) held that award of such bonus marks was unconstitutional and the relevant clause in the circular providing for bonus marks was void.
Whether the award of bonus marks to the applicants belonging to the District and the rural areas of the district concerned is constitutional or not.
Whether the appointments made in conformity with the impugned Circular have been in consonance with law.
Whether any appointment made earlier shall be affected by this judgment and it would have prospective application.
petitioner_arguments: The award of bonus marks to the applicants belonging to the District and the rural areas of the district concerned is unconstitutional and the relevant clause in the circular providing for bonus marks was void.
The appointments made in conformity with the impugned Circular have not been in consonance with law.

No relief can be granted to the petitioners as they could not succeed to get the place in the merit list even by getting 10 bonus marks being residents of urban area, for which they are certainly not entitled.
respondent_arguments: The award of bonus marks to the applicants belonging to the District and the rural areas of the district concerned is constitutional.
The appointments made in conformity with the impugned Circular have been in consonance with law.

No relief can be granted to the petitioners as they could not succeed to get the place in the merit list even by getting 10 bonus marks being residents of urban area, for which they are certainly not entitled.
court_reasoning: The full Bench followed its earlier judgment in Deepak Kumar Suthar Vs. State of Rajasthan (W.P. No. 1917/1995) and disposed of the Writ Petitions on the same terms as in the previous full Bench reference case.
The full Bench observed that 'merely because the employment relates to the Panchayats, that does not make any difference in the light of the law laid down in the full Bench judgment aforementioned'.
The learned Judges observed that 'this kind of weightage would give a complete go-bye to the merit of the candidates and would seriously affect the efficiency of administration/teaching'.

Instead of sending the matter to the appropriate bench, we think it proper to dispose of this petition with a direction that no relief can be granted to the petitioners as they could not succeed to get the place in the merit list even by getting 10 bonus marks being residents of urban area, for which they are certainly not entitled.
More so, the petitioners have not impleaded any person from the select list, not even the last selected candidate.
We clarify that any appointment made earlier shall not be affected by this judgment and it would have prospective application.
holding: The appeals are taken on file and being disposed of by this common Judgment.

No relief can be granted to the petitioners as they could not succeed to get the place in the merit list even by getting 10 bonus marks being residents of urban area, for which they are certainly not entitled.
Any appointment made earlier shall not be affected by this judgment and it would have prospective application.
